witness.text:
The greatest stock
picker in human history would tell you,
with a completely straight face, not to
pick stocks.

comparisons.rationale: Opens with a vivid human context (house bought in 1958, McDonald's breakfast), a scroll-stop paradox, then promises to resolve it: context lean, interrupt and contrarian snapback are all present within the first minute of text.
comparisons.uncertainty: Single analyst reading of stored untimed text; no audio, timing, CTR or retention data.

witness.text:
Because
this isn't really a video about Warren
Buffett, it's a video about which of his
two answers belongs to you.

comparisons.rationale: Opening states the topic, the audience stake and the question to be answered, with a promise of numbers; emotional tone is wry and curious. Clarity high.
comparisons.uncertainty: Single analyst reading of stored untimed text; no audio, timing, CTR or retention data. First-30-second proxy is the first ~700 characters.

witness.text: What Warren Buffett Would Do With $10,000 Today

comparisons.rationale: Title promises what Buffett would do with $10,000; the opening immediately poses exactly that question and defers the answer, so expectation and opening match.
comparisons.uncertainty: Expectation match inferred from text; viewer behaviour unmeasured; inferred only.

witness.text: What Warren Buffett Would Do With $10,000 Today

comparisons.rationale: The title says what Buffett "would do", but the script is built from his past public statements; no new statement from him is shown. Low clickbait risk, small overclaim risk.
comparisons.uncertainty: Inferred audience reaction only; not measured.

comparisons.source_locator: p.1 s.1 ChatGPT; s.6 Google AI Studio

witness.text:
Now, here's
where this video earns its title

comparisons.rationale: The script explicitly marks the pivot to the title promise (the personal small-sum answer) and then resolves both answers. The thumbnail line "ALL YOU NEED IS $10,000" is only partly delivered: the 50% case needs skill and time (script), the index case needs 40 years.
comparisons.uncertainty: Thumbnail/title/script alignment judged from text and image only.

witness.text:
And one of them is going to
surprise you.

comparisons.rationale: Explicit open loop ("one of them is going to surprise you") planted in the first minute and paid off by the 50% a year reveal and the "same answer for two people" resolution.
comparisons.uncertainty: Loop pairing is inferred from text order; retention effect not evaluable.

witness.text:
But
hold on. Before Buffett would put a
single dollar of your 10,000 dollars
into anything, he'd ask you one question

comparisons.rationale: Explicit BUT pivot from the index advice to the debt precondition, then a THEREFORE consequence ("The debt eats first"). Later pivot "Now, here's where this video earns its title".
comparisons.uncertainty: Transition counts are descriptive; ASR text may drop or alter connectives.

witness.text:
A million
dollars in the hedge funds gained about
$220,000.

comparisons.rationale: Specific numbers are present but this one is contradicted by the Berkshire table ($363,000 average-fund gain versus $1,258,000 for the index); specificity here lowers rather than raises credibility. Reference criterion rewards specificity, the fact-check overrides it.
comparisons.uncertainty: Specificity is not accuracy; see packet claim C06.
